subject: Marketplace partnership: residency harmonization & deletion orchestration (AWS/GCP/Azure)
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@stratus-analytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: AvaCloud Partnerships <partner-ops@avacloud.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency & deletion expectations for Marketplace listing

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Stratus is excited to move forward with the Redwood Marketplace listing. Before we start legal and procurement, a few quick questions from our security and SRE teams around residency/retention for the listing across AWS, GCP, and Azure:

- Can you confirm where customer data (request payloads, logs, telemetry) will be stored by default for a marketplace deployment?
- For each cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) do you have a recommended region mapping or a way to enforce region selection per-customer?
- What are your default retention windows for logs and request traces, and is there a configurable TTL per account?
- If a customer requests deletion (or in the case of a marketplace delisting), what is the orchestration timeline and steps — do you purge from backups and object storage, and how do you handle cross-region replicas?

If you already have a short matrix to share that covers region vs storage type vs deletion step, that’d be ideal. Happy to loop in procurement after we align on the technical flow.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of Cloud Ops, Stratus Analytics
---
[Attachment: requirements-stratus-2028-01.pdf (PDF)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@stratus-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, AvaCloud Partnerships <partner-ops@avacloud.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion expectations for Marketplace listing

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear list. I’m attaching a concise residency matrix and a proposed deletion orchestration diagram to get us started. High-level answers below, and I’ll ask Ben to follow up with operational details.

- Default storage: For a hosted marketplace listing via the cloud marketplaces we persist minimal request metadata and tracing logs in the customer-selected region (object storage + time-series metrics). Full request payloads are only stored when the customer opts into request logging for debugging, otherwise payloads are ephemeral (in-memory/KV cache) and not persisted long-term.
- Region mapping: Customers choose region at onboarding; we map marketplace region selection to a best-practice canonical region per cloud (e.g., us-west-2 for AWS, us-central1 for GCP, westus2 for Azure) but we support explicit region locks per customer.
- Retention windows: Default logs/metrics retention is 90 days; request-level payload retention (if enabled) defaults to 30 days. Both are configurable by account and can be shortened to meet customer requirements.
- Deletion orchestration: Deletion requests are executed with a three-stage workflow — mark for deletion (soft delete), purge primary stores (object buckets & databases) within 7 days, and then scrub backups/replicas within 30–45 days depending on backup lifecycle. Cross-region replicas are queued and removed according to the replica owner’s retention policy; we orchestrate replica deletion as part of the same workflow and provide attestations when complete.

See attached matrix for per-cloud specifics (storage endpoints, default regions) and a quick flowchart for deletion steps. Ben — can you add the S3/GCS/Azure Blob semantics and backup timing so I can share this with procurement?

Connor
Senior Partnership Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: residency-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@stratus-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, AvaCloud Partnerships <partner-ops@avacloud.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion expectations for Marketplace listing

Adding the operational specifics Daniel asked for — I kept it concise:

AWS (default us-west-2):
- Storage: S3 (versioned buckets disabled by default for marketplace listings). Metrics in CloudWatch Logs with 90d retention.
- Backups: Nightly EBS snapshots only for Dedicated customers; hosted marketplace uses object lifecycle to transition to colder storage and eventual expiration.
- Deletion flow: Soft-delete flag in metadata store -> S3 object delete + lifecycle immediate expiration (if requested) -> background job reconciles and removes multipart uploads and markers within 24–72h -> final backup/replica scrub queued (30–45d)

GCP (default us-central1):
- Storage: GCS with object holds off by default. Stackdriver/Cloud Monitoring retention 90d.
- Backups: none for hosted listing; we retain exports for 14d for debugging then remove.
- Deletion flow: immediate object deletion request -> GCS lifecycle expires noncurrent generations -> export artifacts removed within 7–14d -> cross-region replicas handled via coordination job

Azure (default westus2):
- Storage: Blob Storage (hot tier), diagnostics to Monitor with 90d retention.
- Backups: optional snapshots for Dedicated.
- Deletion flow: delete blobs + delete container markers -> reconcile index + purge monitoring traces within 7d -> backup scrub queued 30–45d

Notes/constraints:
- Immutable backups maintained under some customer contracts may extend the scrub window; we surface these exceptions in the attestation.
- Marketplace delisting is treated like a customer-initiated deletion for the listed account resources, but marketplace-provided artifacts (listing metadata) are removed according to marketplace storefront policies.

I’ve attached a quick diagram (PNG) of the orchestration window. Let me know if you need timings shortened; we can offer accelerated scrub as an add-on in some enterprise agreements, but it’s subject to storage provider GC windows.

Ben
Senior Cloud Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: deletion-workflow.drawio.png (PNG)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@stratus-analytics.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, AvaCloud Partnerships <partner-ops@avacloud.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion expectations for Marketplace listing

Hi Daniel —

Two legal/contract items to flag before procurement:
1) We can include a binding data residency schedule in the Marketplace listing language that commits to customer-selected region(s) and the deletion orchestration described above. However, we need to align on SLA windows for attestation delivery (we typically provide a certificate of deletion within 30–60 days after the request is fully processed). If your compliance needs a faster attestation, we can scope that in the MSA addendum.
2) Backup exemptions: If Stratus requires immutable backups for regulatory reasons, we must document the hold and the expected extension window (this becomes an exception to the standard purge timeline).

Draft redlines attached (v2) — Connor, feel free to share with Daniel & procurement and we can iterate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships & Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@stratus-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, AvaCloud Partnerships <partner-ops@avacloud.com>, GCP Marketplace Team <gcp-partner@cloudops.example.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jan 2028 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion expectations for Marketplace listing

Marissa, Connor —

Thanks — this is very helpful and addresses most of our questions. A couple of follow-ups before procurement:

- Can you confirm the attestation format (PDF signed, API callback with job id, or uploaded report to customer Drive)? We prefer an auditable PDF with timestamped signature and an API status endpoint that we can poll.
- For the accelerated scrub add-on Ben mentioned: what are the pricing tiers and expected timelines (e.g., 7-day full scrub vs standard 30–45d)?
- One more ask from our security lead: will you provide a short runbook (2–3 pages) describing the deletion orchestration we can keep in our incident binder?

If you can share the attestation sample and pricing note, we’ll loop in procurement and legal next week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Daniel
Director of Cloud Ops, Stratus Analytics
